mainTopic: How to word the תפילה when יום טוב, ראש חודש or חול המועד falls on שבת; making עירובין and baking from one יום טוב day for the next; and the laws of one who did not make an עירובי תבשילין.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier עירוב discussion: רב הונא rules הלכה כרבי ולאיסור, so no עירוב may be made in that case. A ברייתא then asks how to daven when יום טוב falls on שבת. בית שמאי say eight ברכות; בית הלל say seven, with יום טוב mentioned inside the שבת ברכה. רבי adds that the closing line mentions both days, and רב יוסף rules like רבי in the word order רבינא fixed: 'מקדש השבת, ישראל והזמנים'. A second ברייתא teaches that on שבת ראש חודש or חול המועד, the special day is mentioned in רצה (רבי אליעזר says in מודים), and in מוסף it goes inside the שבת ברכה; רב הונא rejects the pair who apply the מוסף structure to every תפילה. רב and רבא then allow making עירובי תחומין or עירובי תבשילין on the first day of יום טוב for the second, with a תנאי, and the גמרא explains why רבא is stricter about תחומין. Next comes a ברייתא on baking from one יום טוב day for the next, where רבא rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that one may fill the whole oven. Finally, the גמרא proves that someone without an עירובי תבשילין is forbidden and so is his flour. It then asks what happens if he baked anyway, and starts a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case brought as proof is itself the bad outcome
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting an earlier proof. The case that was brought could be exactly the קלקול (bad outcome) that the rule was worried about.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the very damage we were worried about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing a rejection it started on the previous amud. The case someone used as proof can be explained as the exact 'damage' that the opposing view feared, so it proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא tried to use a case to decide what the halacha is about making an עירוב on יום טוב before שבת. Here it answers that the case may simply show the problem itself happening. So the proof is knocked out, and the question stays open until the next ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: this is exactly / this is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an argument that started on the previous עמוד. It is not a new topic, so read it as the last word of a rejection.

phrases.english: This is the very damage (we were worried about).
phrases.notes: Closes a דחיה that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the rejection of a proof brought on the previous עמוד.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempted proof about the halacha of עירוב on יום טוב next to שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case cited can be read as the very 'damage' itself, so it does not show what the halacha is.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי, the strict way
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב חסדא, who quotes רב הונא: the halacha follows רבי, and it is the strict version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב חסדא, who said in the name of רב הונא: the halacha follows רבי, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: After the proof was rejected, the גמרא now gives a clear final ruling. We follow רבי, and we follow him in the strict direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two versions of what רבי held. The word 'ולאיסור' tells us which version wins: the strict one. In that version, one may not make an עירוב in this situation at all, neither עירובי חצירות nor עירובי תחומין.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, editor of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling for the עירוב discussion is: הלכה כרבי ולאיסור. Neither type of עירוב may be made in this case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long עירוב discussion with a practical ruling before the גמרא moves on to תפילה.

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Ḥisda said
that Rav Huna said:
The halakha follows Rabbi, and (in the version that) forbids.
phrases.notes: Follows רבי אלעזר's version of רבי's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the proof is rejected, the גמרא states the halacha directly through an אמורא's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows רבי's strict view: no עירוב may be made in this case.

steps.title: בית שמאי: eight ברכות when יום טוב falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא opens a new topic. When יום טוב falls on שבת, בית שמאי say the עמידה has eight ברכות, with a separate ברכה for שבת and a separate one for יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: when יום טוב falls on שבת, בית שמאי say one prays eight ברכות. He says a ברכה for שבת by itself and a ברכה for יום טוב by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a brand-new topic: how to daven when יום טוב and שבת come on the same day. It begins with בית שמאי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת or יום טוב the עמידה normally has seven ברכות: three at the start, three at the end, and one middle ברכה about the special day. בית שמאי hold that when both days come together, each one gets its own middle ברכה. That makes eight ברכות in total.

keyTerms.meaning: by itself, as a separate unit

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A Festival that falls on Shabbat:
Beit Shammai say: one prays eight (blessings),
and says the one for Shabbat by itself,
and the one for the Festival by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. It is connected to the previous one only because both deal with יום טוב next to or on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: eight ברכות, with a separate middle ברכה for שבת and for יום טוב.

steps.title: בית הלל: seven ברכות, with יום טוב inside the שבת ברכה
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל say one prays seven ברכות. The middle ברכה starts and ends with שבת, and the holiness of יום טוב is mentioned in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: one prays seven ברכות. He begins with שבת and ends with שבת, and mentions the holiness of the day (יום טוב) in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives בית הלל's opposing view. Both days share one middle ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל keep the normal seven-ברכה structure. They fit יום טוב inside the שבת ברכה: the ברכה opens about שבת, mentions יום טוב in its body, and closes about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the holiness of the day (the middle ברכה about the special day)

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: one prays seven (blessings),

phrases.aramaic: מַתְחִיל בְּשֶׁל שַׁבָּת וּמְסַיֵּים בְּשֶׁל שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: he begins with that of Shabbat and ends with that of Shabbat,
and says the sanctity of the day (of the Festival) in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: seven ברכות. The middle ברכה begins and ends with שבת, and יום טוב is mentioned inside it.

steps.title: רבי: the closing line mentions both שבת and the festivals
steps.stepSummary: רבי adds that the closing line of the ברכה also mentions יום טוב: 'מקדש השבת, ישראל והזמנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: he even closes the ברכה with it: 'Who sanctifies שבת, ישראל, and the festivals.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי adds a detail to בית הלל's view. The closing line (חתימה) should mention יום טוב as well, not only שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית הלל, the ending was only about שבת. רבי says the ending should include both: 'מקדש השבת' for שבת, and 'ישראל והזמנים' for the festivals.

keyTerms.meaning: closes / seals (the ending line of a ברכה)

phrases.english: Rabbi says: he even concludes with it:
"Who sanctifies Shabbat, Israel, and the seasons."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to בית הלל's view by making the closing line include יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The closing line mentions both days: 'מקדש השבת, ישראל והזמנים'.

steps.title: A different version of רבי's wording is taught before רבינא
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites the ברייתא in front of רבינא with a different word order: 'מקדש ישראל והשבת והזמנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רבינא: 'Who sanctifies ישראל, and שבת, and the festivals.'
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. A reciter quotes רבי's closing line in a different order, and רבינא is about to object to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change is the order: ישראל comes first, before שבת. This order suggests that ישראל make שבת holy. That idea is what רבינא will attack.

keyTerms.meaning: a reciter of memorized ברייתות in the בית מדרש

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Ravina:
"Who sanctifies Israel, and Shabbat, and the seasons."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a competing version of the wording from step 5.

steps.title: רבינא objects: ישראל do not make שבת holy
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the version: do ישראל sanctify שבת? שבת is already holy on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: Is that to say that ישראל make שבת holy? But שבת is already holy and stands that way!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the word order of the version he just heard. It implies something untrue about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ישראל' comes first, the line sounds like 'Who sanctifies ישראל, who in turn sanctify שבת.' But שבת comes every seventh day since בריאת העולם, with no human declaration needed. Only the festivals depend on ישראל, because בית דין sets the calendar.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (introduces a rhetorical challenge)
but surely / but isn't it so
is already sanctified and stands that way

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying ישראל are unimportant. He is saying ישראל are not the ones who make שבת holy. They do, however, set the festivals through the calendar.

phrases.english: He (Ravina) said to him:
Is that to say Israel sanctifies Shabbat?
But Shabbat is already sanctified and stands so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the variant wording of step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That order implies ישראל make שבת holy. But שבת's holiness is fixed from בריאת העולם and does not depend on people.

steps.title: Fix the wording: שבת first, then ישראל and the festivals
steps.stepSummary: רבינא corrects the text: say 'מקדש השבת, ישראל והזמנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'Who sanctifies שבת, ישראל, and the festivals.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא fixes the version so that it no longer suggests ישראל make שבת holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שבת first, ה׳ alone makes שבת holy. Then ה׳ makes ישראל holy, and ישראל in turn make the festivals holy by fixing the calendar. This matches the version of רבי quoted in step 5.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
"Who sanctifies Shabbat, Israel, and the seasons."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבינא's objection by correcting the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (changing the order of words).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The version had ישראל before שבת, implying ישראל sanctify שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת comes first because it is holy on its own. ישראל, who are made holy by ה׳, then sanctify the festivals.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the halacha follows רבי, as רבינא fixed it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the halacha follows רבי's closing line, in the form רבינא corrected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the halacha follows רבי, and as רבינא corrected it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling on how to close the ברכה when יום טוב falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to the ruling. First, we follow רבי, so the closing line mentions both שבת and the festivals. Second, we use רבינא's word order, with שבת before ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: When יום טוב falls on שבת: seven ברכות, as בית הלל say. The closing line is 'מקדש השבת, ישראל והזמנים', following רבי and רבינא's order.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the closing line we still say today in the יום טוב עמידה when it falls on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halakha follows Rabbi, and as Ravina resolved (the wording).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי, וְכִדְתָרֵיץ רָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes רבי's view, as corrected by רבינא, the final halacha.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ending is 'מקדש השבת, ישראל והזמנים'.

steps.title: שבת on ראש חודש or חול המועד: seven ברכות, with mention in עבודה
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: when שבת falls on ראש חודש or חול המועד, מעריב, שחרית and מנחה have seven ברכות. The special day is mentioned in the עבודה ברכה (רצה). If one forgot, he must repeat the תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: when שבת falls on ראש חודש or on חול המועד, in ערבית, שחרית and מנחה one prays seven ברכות. He says something about the special event in the עבודה ברכה. If he did not say it, he must go back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא deals with a smaller special day, ראש חודש or חול המועד, falling on שבת. It explains where to mention that day in the regular תפילות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These days do not get their own middle ברכה in these תפילות. Instead, a short insert about the day (יעלה ויבא) goes into רצה, the עבודה ברכה. Forgetting it is serious enough that one must repeat the תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: the intermediate days of a festival (חול המועד)
something matching the occasion (e.g., יעלה ויבא)
the ברכה of רצה, about the עבודה in the בית המקדש
we make him go back and repeat

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Shabbat that falls on a New Moon
or on the intermediate days of a Festival,
in the evening, morning, and afternoon prayers, one prays seven (blessings),
and says a passage matching the occasion in the Temple-service blessing,
and if he did not say it, we make him go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related new case: a lesser special day, rather than יום טוב, coinciding with שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven ברכות, with the insert in רצה. If forgotten, one repeats the תפילה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the insert goes in הודאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees about the location and says the insert goes in the הודאה ברכה (מודים).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: in the הודאה ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the ברייתא about where to place the insert. He puts it in מודים instead of רצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the day must be mentioned. The only disagreement is which ברכה it belongs in: עבודה (רצה) according to the תנא קמא, or הודאה (מודים) according to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: in the thanksgiving (blessing).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissent on one detail of step 10: the location of the insert.

steps.title: In מוסף: start and end with שבת, the special day in the middle
steps.stepSummary: In מוסף, the middle ברכה begins and ends with שבת, and the holiness of ראש חודש or the מועד is mentioned in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in מוסף, he begins with שבת and ends with שבת, and says the holiness of the day in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining מוסף, where the special day gets fuller mention inside the middle ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוסף is centered on the special day's קרבן, so a short insert is not enough. The same structure בית הלל used in step 4 is applied here: open with שבת, mention the special day in the body, and close with שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: שבת with ראש חודש or חול המועד: in ערבית, שחרית and מנחה, add יעלה ויבא in רצה (רבי אליעזר: in מודים). In מוסף, the special day goes inside the שבת ברכה.

phrases.english: And in the additional prayers he begins with that of Shabbat
and ends with that of Shabbat,
and says the sanctity of the day in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main voice of the ברייתא (after רבי אליעזר's dissent) to give the rule for מוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוסף: begin and end with שבת, with the special day's holiness in the middle.

steps.title: A second opinion: open and close with שבת in every seven-ברכה תפילה
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא say that wherever seven ברכות are said, the middle ברכה begins and ends with שבת, and the special day is mentioned in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, say: in any תפילה that needs seven ברכות, one begins the middle ברכה with שבת, ends it with שבת, and mentions the holiness of the special day in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more תנאים add their opinion. They say the מוסף method should be used in every seven-ברכה תפילה, not only in מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (Step 10) said that in מעריב, שחרית and מנחה the special day is mentioned in רצה. This pair disagrees. They say the middle ברכה should be built like מוסף (Step 12): it opens with שבת, closes with שבת, and mentions ראש חודש or the מועד in between.

keyTerms.meaning: the holiness of the day (here, ראש חודש or the מועד)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, say:
Wherever one is required to say seven blessings,
phrases.notes: This includes מעריב, שחרית and מנחה, not only מוסף.

phrases.english: he begins the middle blessing with Shabbat
and concludes it with Shabbat
and mentions the holiness of the day in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the מוסף structure from Step 12 and applies it to every seven-ברכה תפילה, disagreeing with the first opinion in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In every seven-ברכה תפילה on שבת that is also ראש חודש or a מועד, the middle ברכה opens and closes with שבת, and the special day is mentioned in the middle.

steps.title: רב הונא rules against this pair
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the הלכה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the הלכה is not like that pair of scholars.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the practical ruling: we do not follow the pair from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the pair is rejected, the first opinion (Step 10) stands. In מעריב, שחרית and מנחה, the special day is mentioned in רצה. Only מוסף uses the open-and-close-with-שבת structure.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלכה is not (like this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, on שבת ראש חודש or שבת חול המועד, the special day is mentioned in רצה in מעריב, שחרית and מנחה. Only מוסף's middle ברכה opens and closes with שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halacha is not in accordance with that pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the opinion of Step 13 as the practical הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the first opinion: in the regular seven-ברכה תפילות, the special day is mentioned in רצה.

steps.title: רב: one may make עירובי תחומין on the first day of יום טוב for the second, with a stipulation
steps.stepSummary: A new topic. רב rules that a person may place עירובי תחומין on the first day of יום טוב for the next day, using a תנאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: a person may place an עירובי תחומין on one day of יום טוב for the next day, and make a stipulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. In חוץ לארץ, when the two days of יום טוב are Thursday and Friday and someone forgot to make an עירוב beforehand, רב allows him to make it on the first day, with a stipulation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two days are kept because of a doubt about which one is really יום טוב, so one of them is really a weekday. The person says: 'If today is the real יום טוב, I don't need this עירוב for tomorrow. If today is a weekday, then this עירוב is made today for tomorrow.' He repeats the same תנאי on the second day so the עירוב will also work for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: an עירוב that extends how far one may walk beyond the town on שבת or יום טוב
here: for the next day (literally 'for its fellow')
the second day of יום טוב kept outside ארץ ישראל because of doubt

steps.confusionAlert: 'לחבירו' here does NOT mean 'for his friend.' It means one יום טוב day for its 'fellow' day, the next day of יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two days of יום טוב in חוץ לארץ can be treated as one real day and one weekday, and this is what makes the תנאי work.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
A person may place an eiruv for joining boundaries
on one Festival day for the next, and stipulate.
phrases.notes: The stipulation: if today is יום טוב, tomorrow is a weekday and needs no עירוב; if today is a weekday, the עירוב is made today for tomorrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב מַנִּיחַ אָדָם עֵירוּבֵי תְחוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the laws of davening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may place עירובי תחומין on the first day of יום טוב for the second day, using a תנאי based on the doubt about which day is the real יום טוב.

steps.title: רבא: the same works for עירובי תבשילין
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a person may place עירובי תבשילין on the first day of יום טוב for the next day, using a תנאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a person may place an עירובי תבשילין on one day of יום טוב for the next day, and make a stipulation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a parallel ruling. This one is about the עירוב that allows cooking on יום טוב (Friday) for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנאי works the same way: 'If today is a weekday and tomorrow is יום טוב, this is my עירוב so I can cook tomorrow for שבת. If today is יום טוב, tomorrow is a weekday and I can cook anyway.' The next step compares how far each ruling reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: a cooked dish set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person may place an eiruv for joining cooked foods
on one Festival day for the next, and stipulate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא מַנִּיחַ אָדָם עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same ruling as Step 15, but for עירובי תבשילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may place עירובי תבשילין on the first day of יום טוב for the second day, using a תנאי.

steps.title: Comparing the two rulings: one goes further than the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that whoever permits עירובי תחומין surely permits עירובי תבשילין, but whoever permits עירובי תבשילין does not necessarily permit עירובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said this about עירובי תחומין would certainly say it about עירובי תבשילין. But the one who said it about עירובי תבשילין would not say it about עירובי תחומין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares רב and רבא to see how far each one goes. This sets up the question of why there is a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירובי תחומין is the stricter case. So רב, who permits it, would surely permit the easier case of עירובי תבשילין (a כל שכן). But רבא, who spoke only about תבשילין, forbids תחומין.

phrases.english: The one who said this about the eiruv for joining boundaries —
all the more so the eiruv for joining cooked foods,
but the one who said this about the eiruv for joining cooked foods —
however, the eiruv for joining boundaries, not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר עֵירוּבֵי תְחוּמִין כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the rulings of Steps 15 and 16 and shows that one goes further than the other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling includes עירובי תבשילין, but רבא's ruling does not include עירובי תחומין.

steps.title: Why is עירובי תחומין stricter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא would forbid עירובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why עירובי תחומין should be stricter than עירובי תבשילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both עירובין use the same kind of תנאי, so it is not obvious why one would be allowed and the other forbidden. The גמרא wants the logic behind the difference.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the difference described in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why עירובי תחומין may not be made on יום טוב with a תנאי, while עירובי תבשילין may.

steps.title: Acquiring a resting place on a day of rest is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: The answer: acquiring שביתה (a legal resting place) on a day of rest was not permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one may not acquire a resting place on a day of rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עירובי תחומין works by acquiring a new legal 'home base,' and doing that on a day of rest is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירובי תחומין actually creates a legal acquisition of a new resting place (שביתה), so it was not allowed on יום טוב, even when there is a doubt. עירובי תבשילין is only a symbolic reminder, so it was allowed for the honor of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a legal 'resting place' or home base for measuring the תחום
here: a day of rest (יום טוב), not specifically שבת

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשבתא' here refers to יום טוב, a day of rest in general, not the weekly שבת. The case is the first day of יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: רב permits both עירובין with a תנאי. רבא permits only עירובי תבשילין, because acquiring שביתה on a day of rest is not allowed.

phrases.english: Because acquiring a place of residence on a day of rest is not permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עירובי תחומין is a real acquisition of שביתה, which is forbidden on a day of rest. עירובי תבשילין is not, so it is allowed with a תנאי.

steps.title: A ברייתא: no baking from one יום טוב for the next
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that one may not bake on one day of יום טוב for the following day. Filling a whole pot with meat, or a whole barrel with water, is allowed even if only a little is needed. Baking, however, is limited to what is needed for that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not bake on one day of יום טוב for the next. Truly they said: A woman may fill a whole pot with meat, even though she needs only one piece. A baker may fill a whole barrel of water, even though he needs only one jug. But for baking, he bakes only what he needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the theme of preparing on the first day of יום טוב for the second day. It sets limits on cooking and baking extra food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that cooking on יום טוב is allowed only for that same day. Adding meat to a pot or water to a barrel that is already being heated involves no real extra work, so it is permitted. Baking is different, because each extra loaf is a separate act of work, so one may bake only what is needed for today.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Truly they said; introduces an established הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the pot and barrel cases allow cooking for tomorrow on purpose. They are allowed only because the extra amount is added within one single act of cooking.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not bake from one Festival day for the next.
phrases.notes: For example, from the first day of יום טוב for the second day kept in חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: Truly they said:
A woman may fill the entire pot with meat,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה אֶלָּא לַחֲתִיכָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: even though she needs only one piece.
A baker may fill a barrel of water,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ אֶלָּא לְקִיתוֹן אֶחָד.
phrases.english: even though he needs only one jug.
But regarding baking —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹפֶה אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁצָּרִיךְ לוֹ.
phrases.english: he bakes only what he needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין אוֹפִין מִיּוֹם טוֹב לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of preparing on one day of יום טוב for the next, now applied to cooking and baking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No baking on one day of יום טוב for the next. Extra meat in one pot or extra water in one barrel is allowed, but baking is limited to that day's needs.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר permits filling the whole oven
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a woman may fill the entire oven with bread, because bread bakes better in a full oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: A woman may fill the whole oven with bread, because bread bakes well when the oven is full.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא disagrees with the limit on baking. It allows filling the whole oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full oven holds its heat better, so the extra loaves also improve today's bread. The extra baking therefore helps the food eaten today and is not only for tomorrow. That is why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר treats it like the full pot of meat.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
A woman may fill the entire oven with bread,
because bread bakes well
when the oven is full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's limit on baking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may fill the whole oven, since a full oven bakes even today's bread better.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the practical ruling between the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a person may fill the oven completely on יום טוב. The reason is that the extra loaves improve the bread being eaten that same day.
steps.whatToRemember: Normally you may not bake on one day of יום טוב for the next. But filling the whole oven is allowed, because a full oven bakes today's bread better (רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement between Steps 20 and 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: one may fill the whole oven.

steps.title: Without עירובי תבשילין, is the person forbidden or also his flour?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about someone who did not make an עירובי תבשילין. Is only the person forbidden to cook for שבת, or is his flour also forbidden from being prepared?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked: One who did not set aside an עירובי תבשילין — is he forbidden and his flour forbidden? Or perhaps he is forbidden but his flour is not forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a person who forgot to make an עירובי תבשילין. It asks whether the restriction is on the person or also on his food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירובי תבשילין, a person may not cook on יום טוב for שבת. The question is about the nature of this restriction. Does it apply to him personally, or does it also attach to his ingredients, so that no one may cook them for him?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
A cooked food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
one who did not set aside an eiruv tavshilin,
is he forbidden and his flour forbidden,
or perhaps:
he is forbidden but his flour is not forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, linked to the earlier discussion of עירובי תבשילין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the restriction from lacking an עירובי תבשילין applies only to the person, or also to his food.

steps.title: What practical difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference this question makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask why this question matters in practice. It is setting up the next step, which explains the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before trying to solve the question, the גמרא wants to see a real case where the two sides would lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what is there a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the question in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where the two sides of the question would differ.

steps.title: The difference: must he transfer his flour to others?
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether he must transfer ownership of his flour to others so they can bake it. If his flour is forbidden, he must transfer it. If only he is forbidden, he does not need to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is about transferring his flour to others. If you say he and his flour are both forbidden, he must transfer his flour to others. If you say only he is forbidden and not his flour, he does not need to transfer his flour to others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is whether he must give his flour to other people (who did make an עירוב) so that they can bake for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the flour itself is forbidden, others may bake it only once it truly belongs to them. Then they can give him the bread. If only the person is forbidden, others may bake his flour while it still belongs to him.

phrases.english: Regarding transferring his flour to others.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ הוּא נֶאֱסָר וְקִמְחוֹ נֶאֱסָר —
phrases.english: If you say he is forbidden and his flour is forbidden —
he must transfer his flour to others.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ הוּא נֶאֱסָר וְאֵין קִמְחוֹ נֶאֱסָר —
phrases.english: And if you say he is forbidden but his flour is not forbidden —
he need not transfer his flour to others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in Step 24 for a practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether he must transfer ownership of his flour to others before they bake it for him.

steps.title: So what is the law?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the practical difference is clear, the גמרא asks again what the answer is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question and asks which side is correct. This sets up the attempts to resolve it that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is now fully defined, with a real practical result. The גמרא is ready to look for a source that decides it.

phrases.english: What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the original question after defining its practical result.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether only the person is forbidden, or also his flour.

steps.title: A ברייתא answers the question about his flour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. Someone without an עירובי תבשילין may not bake, cook, or insulate food, either for himself or for others. Others may not cook for him either. His only option is to transfer ownership of his flour to others, and then they bake for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A person who did not place an עירובי תבשילין may not bake, cook, or insulate food, not for himself and not for others. Others also may not bake or cook for him. So what can he do? He gives his flour over to others, and they bake and cook for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question from Step 26: is only the person forbidden, or is his flour forbidden too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key line is that others may not cook for him while the flour is still his. He has to transfer ownership first. If only the person were forbidden, others could simply bake his flour for him. Since he must give the flour away, the flour itself must be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; the גמרא is bringing a source to answer the question
Food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת
Insulate or wrap food to keep it warm

steps.confusionAlert: He is not selling the flour away for good. He transfers ownership so that others can legally bake it, and the food they bake is then for him to eat on שבת.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who did not place an eiruv tavshilin,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יֹאפֶה וְלֹא יְבַשֵּׁל וְלֹא יַטְמִין,
phrases.english: he may not bake, nor cook, nor insulate food,
not for himself and not for others.
And others may not bake and cook for him.
What should he do?
He transfers ownership of his flour to others,
phrases.notes: This is the line the proof depends on.

phrases.english: and they bake for him and cook for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repeated question of Step 26 using a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the flour itself is forbidden, or only the person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring him to transfer his flour to others before they bake for him.

steps.title: Conclusion: both the person and his flour are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that both the person and his flour are forbidden, and it confirms this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: he is forbidden, and his flour is forbidden. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא requires transferring the flour, the flour itself carries the איסור. The question from Step 23 is now fully settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; said first as an inference, then repeated as confirmation

steps.whatToRemember: Without an עירובי תבשילין, both the person and his flour are forbidden. The fix is to transfer the flour to others, who then bake for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practical advice of transferring ownership of the flour (מקנה קמחו לאחרים).

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: הוּא נֶאֱסָר וְקִמְחוֹ נֶאֱסָר,
phrases.english: Learn from this: he is forbidden and his flour is forbidden.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: הוּא נֶאֱסָר וְקִמְחוֹ נֶאֱסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in Step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both he and his flour are forbidden.

steps.title: New question: what if he baked anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question. If someone without an עירובי תבשילין broke the rule and baked, what is the law about that food?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he went ahead and baked anyway, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about after-the-fact (בדיעבד) cases: is the food he baked allowed or forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the discussion was about what he is allowed to do from the start. Now the question is what happens once the rule has already been broken. Does the food he baked against the rule become forbidden, or may it be used for שבת?

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; introduces a real unresolved question
After the fact; once the act has already been done

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If he transgressed and baked, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling that the flour is forbidden, the גמרא asks about the after-the-fact case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether food baked without an עירובי תבשילין is permitted after the fact.

steps.title: Starting a proof from the same ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again. A person without an עירובי תבשילין must transfer his flour to others, who then bake and cook for him. The גמרא is setting up a proof about the after-the-fact question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A person who did not place an עירובי תבשילין, what should he do? He transfers his flour to others, and they bake and cook for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof to answer the new question. It quotes the ברייתא, and the inference from it will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is quoted again for a new purpose. Before, it proved that the flour is forbidden. Now the focus is on the fact that the ברייתא gives him a workaround at all. The גמרא is preparing to ask: if baking anyway were acceptable after the fact, why would he need this workaround?

keyTerms.meaning: How should he act? The ברייתא's way of offering a solution

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a repeat of Step 27. The same ברייתא is being used to answer a different question: the after-the-fact case.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who did not place an eiruv tavshilin,
what should he do?
He transfers ownership of his flour to others,
and the others bake for him and cook for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין, כֵּיצַד הוּא עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 29 by quoting the ברייתא again.
steps.raayaObject: Whether food baked without an עירובי תבשילין is permitted after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's instruction to transfer the flour, which suggests that simply baking anyway would not work.
